questions.scenario: Your class is making a Farewell Video for the 12th standard seniors. What is your main job?

options.A: I am running around the school corridors with my phone, getting dynamic low-angle shots of the seniors.
options.B: I take all the rough video clips home and spend hours stitching them together with a nostalgic Bollywood song.
options.C: I decide the 'saree and suit' dress code and find the most aesthetic, sunlit spot in the school for the shoot.
options.D: I convince the strict Principal for permission, tell everyone what to say, and manage the whole shooting schedule.

questions.scenario: It is your best friend's birthday and you are making an Instagram Reel for them. How do you approach it?

options.A: I get on my knees to shoot the perfect slow-motion video of them blowing out the candles.
options.B: I carefully sync every single beat drop of a trending Punjabi song to different funny clips of them.
options.C: I am busy decorating the room with fairy lights, balloons, and making sure the cake looks highly photogenic.
options.D: I make sure all friends arrive for the surprise exactly on time and coordinate who brings what gift.

questions.scenario: You are watching a massive blockbuster Bollywood movie in the theatre. What distracts you the most?

options.A: Trying to figure out how they moved the camera so smoothly during a high-speed car chase.
options.B: Noticing a continuity mistake, like a glass being half-full and then magically full in the very next second.
options.C: Obsessing over the hero's styling, the grand palatial sets, and the beautiful background colors.
options.D: Thinking about how much money it cost to make the film and how the director got the actors to cry so naturally.

questions.scenario: It's a family wedding (Shaadi) and the cousins are preparing for the Sangeet dance. What are you doing?

options.A: Following the professional photographer 'bhaiya' around and taking my own cinematic portraits of the bride.
options.B: Making a hilarious slideshow of the couple's childhood photos to play on the big LED screen during the performances.
options.C: Picking the perfect matching outfits for all the cousins and suggesting cool props like sunglasses or colorful dupattas.
options.D: Choreographing the dance, putting the best dancers in the front, and scolding everyone who misses practice.

questions.scenario: Your school is hosting a Diwali Mela and you have to create a promotional video. What's your role?

options.A: Walking through the crowded stalls with my camera gimbal, getting moving shots of people eating jalebis.
options.B: Adding cool text effects, color-grading the video to look warm, and removing the noisy background crowd audio.
options.C: Decorating our class stall with diyas, rangoli, and handmade posters so it looks incredible on camera.
options.D: Writing the script for the video, making the teachers say a few words, and telling the host where to stand.

questions.scenario: You are part of the school's Annual Day Drama. Even if you aren't acting, how are you involved?

options.A: Handling the spotlight from the balcony, making sure the main character is always perfectly lit.
options.B: Operating the laptop soundboard, triggering the dramatic thunder sound effects exactly when the villain enters.
options.C: Painting the cardboard trees, arranging the stage props, and deciding the makeup for the kings and queens.
options.D: Holding the script, shouting 'Action' during rehearsals, and getting the actors to show more emotion.

questions.scenario: You just got a brand new smartphone with an amazing camera. What is the very first thing you do?

options.A: Test the zoom, try out portrait mode, and physically move around the house taking close-ups of pets or plants.
options.B: Download three different video editing apps and test out the slow-motion, reverse, and glitch effects.
options.C: Arrange your study table perfectly with a coffee mug and a book to click the ultimate 'aesthetic' picture.
options.D: Call your friends to come over immediately so you can start planning a mini vlog or sketch comedy video together.

questions.scenario: You are watching a daily soap TV serial with your family. What annoys you the absolute most?

options.A: The camera zooming in and out aggressively 10 times on the mother-in-law's face.
options.B: The loud 'Dhoom Tana' sound effects that don't match the scene, or terrible green-screen backgrounds.
options.C: The tacky heavy jewelry, overly bright makeup, and fake-looking plastic flowers in the house.
options.D: The terrible acting by the main lead and the completely senseless, dragging storyline.

questions.scenario: During a group project presentation in class, what is your hidden superpower?

options.A: Setting up the projector physically and making sure the slides are clearly visible from every angle.
options.B: Formatting the PowerPoint so everything aligns perfectly, adding smooth, professional transition effects.
options.C: Designing the title slide with the perfect fonts, borders, and a matching color theme.
options.D: Delegating who speaks which slide and keeping the group strictly under the 5-minute time limit.

questions.scenario: Your housing society is organizing a fancy dress competition for the colony kids. What is your contribution?

options.A: I volunteer to be the official photographer, crouching near the stage to get the best angles of the kids.
options.B: I sit with my laptop and curate the ultimate music playlist, ensuring smooth fading between songs.
options.C: I help the kids put on their superhero capes, fix their props, and touch up their makeup before they go on stage.
options.D: I hold the mic, act as the energetic anchor, and manage the chaotic backstage so kids go on stage in the right order.

Cinematographer.title: Cinematographer / Cameraman
Cinematographer.primary_match_text: The Visual Ninja! You love being on your feet, finding the perfect angles, and capturing the world through a lens.
Cinematographer.day_in_the_life: Operating heavy, expensive cameras, playing with lenses, physically moving around movie sets, and working with lighting teams to capture stunning visuals.
Cinematographer.alternative_match_text: Wildlife Photographer, Drone Operator, Sports Cameraperson
Cinematographer.roadmap: 11th/12th (Any Stream) -> Bachelor of Mass Media (BMM) or BA in Film & TV -> Diploma/Specialization in Cinematography from institutes like FTII or Whistling Woods.

Film_Editor.title: Film Editor / Post-Production
Film_Editor.primary_match_text: The Magic Maker! You have immense patience, an eye for detail, and the technical skills to turn raw footage into a masterpiece.
Film_Editor.day_in_the_life: Sitting in a dark studio with multiple monitors, cutting out bad takes, matching audio beats, color grading, and adding amazing VFX to make the story flow smoothly.
Film_Editor.roadmap: 11th/12th (Any Stream) -> BSc in Animation & VFX OR BA in Mass Communication -> Advanced Certification in Video Editing (Premiere Pro, Final Cut Pro).

Art_Director.title: Art Director / Set Designer
Art_Director.primary_match_text: The Aesthetic Genius! You care deeply about colors, moods, props, and how everything looks on screen.
Art_Director.day_in_the_life: Designing massive movie sets, choosing the color palette of a film, deciding what clothes the actors wear, and making sure the entire movie looks beautiful and authentic.
Art_Director.alternative_match_text: Costume Designer, Production Designer, Interior Stylist
Art_Director.roadmap: 11th/12th (Any Stream, Arts preferred) -> Bachelor of Fine Arts (BFA) or Bachelor of Design (B.Des) -> Specialization in Production Design or Art Direction.

Director_Producer.title: Film Director / Producer
Director_Producer.primary_match_text: The Captain of the Ship! You are a natural leader with a big vision, capable of managing teams and telling powerful stories.
Director_Producer.day_in_the_life: Shouting 'Action' on set, guiding actors on how to deliver dialogues, managing the film's budget, and coordinating with hundreds of crew members to bring your vision to life.
Director_Producer.roadmap: 11th/12th (Any Stream) -> BA in Mass Communication / BMM -> PG Diploma in Film Direction or Production from top institutes like FTII, NSD, or SRFTI -> Years of assisting directors on set.
